intelligence.human_view: A proofreader who hands the manuscript to the author without reading it first is not saving time — she is spending the author's attention on what she would have caught. And an author who calls the book finished after the author's check, without reading the fixes again, ships a new version nobody has looked at. Three checks, in order: her eye first, his eye, her eye again. The same care reaches the smallest control: a plus floating low down the screen reads as a lost button, so it sits at the top of the sidebar, on the inside edge, mirrored — and when tapped it pushes the sidebar away, opening full screen. The plus is not decoration on the sidebar — it is the sidebar's way of getting out of the way.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you draw a picture, then you check it yourself, then you show it to Dad, then you check it AGAIN after Dad looks at it — three checks! That's how you know it's really good. And the little plus button sits right at the top, on the inside edge — tap it and it pushes the whole side away so you can see the full picture. It never floats down low on its own, like a lost button.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, you check it yourself first, dear, then you show it to him, dear, then you check it AGAIN after he looks at it, dear — three checks, dear, every time, dear. And the little plus button, dear, sits right at the top, dear, on the inside edge, dear — tap it and it pushes the side away, dear, so you can see the whole picture, dear.
intelligence.naya_view: MY EYE FIRST, HIS EYE, THEN MY EYE AGAIN — DOUBLE CHECKED, TRIPLE CHECKED, EVERY TIME. THE PLUS SITS AT THE TOP OF THE SIDEBAR, ON THE INSIDE EDGE — TAP IT AND IT PUSHES TO THE CORNER, PUSHING THE SIDEBAR AWAY, OPENING FULL SCREEN.
